---------------------------------------------------------------------
From: Mark Atwood <mark@reviewcommit.com>
To: jmap@ietf.org
Subject: Proposal: localized display text, text handling, URIs and problem details for JMAP (draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00)

Hi all,

While writing JMAP extensions for chat I kept running into the same
gaps in the existing specs, so I've written one draft that tries to
close them for all of JMAP, not just my extensions. Before going
further I'd like to know whether the WG wants this, and whether some
of it belongs in an RFC 8620bis instead.

Draft (editor's copy):
https://github.com/MarkAtwood/jmap-chat-spec/blob/main/draft-atwood-jmap-updates-00.md

Header: Standards Track, Updates: 8620, 9425.

What RFC 8620 already gets right, and the draft keeps: I-JSON/UTF-8
(1.5), Accept-Language and Content-Language for server-chosen strings
(3.8), and collation on /query with collationAlgorithms in the core
capability (5.5). Mail content already carries its own charset and
language, and JSCalendar and JSContact objects already have
localizations.

The gaps, and what the draft does about them:

1. Display text has one value and no language. A shared AddressBook,
   Calendar, Principal or Mailbox has a single name, and nothing says
   what language it is in. The draft adds a capability,
   urn:ietf:params:jmap:i18n, that gives those types the JSCalendar
   `locale` and `localizations` properties (RFC 8984 4.2.8 and 4.6.1),
   limited to a listed set of localizable properties:
     Mailbox: name
     Quota: name, description
     AddressBook: name, description
     Principal: name, description
     Calendar (once published): name, description
   Identity and ParticipantIdentity are deliberately left out: their
   name is the sender's own name, so it should not change with the
   reader's language.

2. Asking for one language. /get, /query and /queryChanges take a
   `language` argument: a list of language ranges, matched against the
   available languages by RFC 4647 Lookup. Accept-Language deliberately
   does NOT change /get results for these properties (MUST NOT). If it
   did, a client caching objects by state would end up with a mix of
   languages it can't tell apart. This is why the draft updates 9425:
   for clients that opt in, `language` replaces Accept-Language
   selection of the Quota description.

3. Text with no request in progress. An optional account-level
   `preferredLanguages` lets a server pick a language for text it
   writes with no request in progress, such as push notification text.
   How it is set is left to the deployment.

4. Text handling, for all of JMAP (no wire change, SHOULD-level):
   - no control characters except LF in display text
   - servers don't normalize stored text; clients send NFC
   - display text carries no meaning (Mailbox role is the model)
   - length limits are in octets, and truncation happens on grapheme
     cluster boundaries
   - text filters compare using the sort collation
   - wall-clock times carry IANA time zone IDs

5. URIs and problem details, for all of JMAP (SHOULD-level):
   - URI-valued properties are RFC 3986 URIs, with IRIs mapped per
     RFC 3987.
   - RFC 8620's references to RFC 7807 become RFC 9457.
   - Every JMAP HTTP resource returns problem details on 4xx/5xx,
     including the Session resource, the event source, the WebSocket
     handshake, and extension endpoints, which 8620 doesn't cover today.

Questions for the WG:

a. Is there interest in this as a WG item? Or would you rather fold
   parts 4 and 5 (and maybe the `language` argument) into an RFC 8620
   revision, and keep only the localization capability as an
   extension?
b. Is "Accept-Language never changes /get data" right? It departs from
   how RFC 9425 handles Quota description.
c. Is the localizable-property list right? Is anything missing, for
   example VacationResponse, whose language would depend on each
   incoming message?
d. Is a single draft that updates 8620 and 9425 acceptable, or would
   you prefer separate documents?

Comments are welcome on the list or as issues on the repo.

Thanks,
Mark Atwood
